trigger.name: sweep
trigger.means: The sweep applies due task timers to tasks no command has touched and fires the workspace timers, through the same code as the timers a command applies first (L118, L820). It is not a timer and writes no event.

due_at.plus: the check's queue timeout: rule_versions.queue_timeout_seconds, or workspaces.check_queue_timeout_seconds when that is null
the check's run timeout: rule_versions.run_timeout_seconds, or workspaces.check_run_timeout_seconds when that is null
the workspace's check queue timeout (plan DB-31)
the workspace's check run timeout (plan DB-31)
the workspace's check queue timeout (plan DB-31)
the workspace's check run timeout (plan DB-31)

none: at once (the task's last effective time) when one of the seat's candidates that may take the task is available; otherwise the earliest limited_until among its signed-in candidates that may take the task, never before the task's last effective time; no due time when none has one. Computed at each look, so a change of credentials needs no write (milestone 3 plan HE-23, rule 8 of section 2.1)
90 seconds, read for each role that claims jobs
none: it runs on every sweep (plan SM-42)
7 days, the least time idempotency keys are kept (L818)

timers.note: It purges command rows past retention and writes no event.

due_at.plus: none: it runs on every sweep (milestone 3 plan HD-4)

timers.note: It moves an idle seat's run to its first available candidate and starts again a run that ended for a limit or a sign-out, through start_seat helper requests; it writes no event.
